subject: Performance SLO / context window follow-up (latency, concurrency, streaming)
messages:
From: Aaron Lee <aaron.lee@finco.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Samantha Ortiz <samantha.ortiz@finco.com>
Date: Mon, 3 Aug 2026 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Performance SLO / context window details

Thanks again for the call today — quick recap from our side and a few follow-ups so we can lock the PoC test matrix. High level: FinCo needs predictable p95 latency under load for user-facing chat and a higher-throughput async batch path for nightly enrichment. A few concrete questions: 1) Target latency: we're aiming for p95 <= 150ms for short multi-turn chats (typical payload ~1.5k input tokens, ~200 output tokens). Is that feasible with an 8k context model? 2) Context window / max tokens: we plan to send up to 6k input tokens (user history + doc snippets) and expect ~1k output in some flows — how does that impact latency and cost? 3) Streaming: we want to stream partial outputs to the client to reduce perceived latency — does Redwood's runtime support chunked/streaming token flushes and what is the expected end-to-end latency for first-byte vs completion? 4) Concurrency/throughput: expected TPS for our pilot is ~20 requests/sec (peak), concurrency target 40 concurrent chat sessions; we also have a batch job that will push 200 reqs/min for long outputs. Any guidance on concurrency knobs, batching, and recommended GPU configs? 5) Can you share sample latency numbers (p50/p95/p99) for 8k and 32k contexts for similar models? Attached is a sample request we'll use (finco_sample_request.json).

Next steps from our side: we can stand up a short pilot environment and run your suggested test harness. Can Redwood run an initial baseline so we can align on what to expect in the PoC?

— Aaron
Aaron Lee
Senior Engineering Manager, FinCo
aaron.lee@finco.com



From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Aaron Lee <aaron.lee@finco.com>
Cc: Samantha Ortiz <samantha.ortiz@finco.com>
Date: Mon, 3 Aug 2026 17:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Performance SLO / context window details

Aaron — great to meet today. Appreciate the clear requirements; below is a short recap plus proposed test plan so we can align on PoC expectations.

Recap / answers:
- Latency targets: For an 8k context, p95 <= 150ms is aggressive but potentially achievable with the right model variant and streaming enabled for first-bytes. For cold KV-cache paths or very large outputs (>=1k tokens) expect higher p95 (300–600ms). We recommend an initial SLO of p95 <= 250ms for the full-request completion for the 6k-in/1k-out profile, and p95 <= 150ms for first-byte (streaming) on typical short-turn chats (~1.5k in / 200 out).
- Context window impact: Latency scales approximately linearly with the attended sequence length in the self-attention and KV cache usage. Going from 8k -> 32k can increase per-request latency by ~2.5–4x depending on kernel selection and whether the request benefits from KV-cache reuse.
- Streaming: Redwood supports streaming token-by-token flushes (Server-Sent Events / chunked HTTP). First-byte latency for streaming is dominated by model decoding for the first token (~30–120ms depending on model & quantization), while completion latency will follow the per-token decode time times output length. Streaming reduces perceived latency significantly and allows you to set a first-byte SLO separate from completion.
- Concurrency & throughput: For your pilot (20 RPS, 40 concurrent chat sessions), recommended starting point is 2 dedicated GPUs of the recommended family (we'll propose exact SKU after we confirm model/quant). Use request-level concurrency limit 2–4 per GPU for multi-turn chat; enable continuous batching with a target batch window of 8–12ms to reduce per-token cost while keeping p95 reasonable. For the async batch job (200 reqs/min), use a separate queue with higher batching tolerance.
- Baseline numbers: Attached is a short baseline PDF that shows p50/p95/p99 numbers across 1k/8k/32k contexts on our recommended model family (redwood_latency_baseline.pdf). We'll run an apples-to-apples baseline using your finco_sample_request.json as the input.

Proposed PoC test matrix:
1) Short-turn chat (1.5k in / 200 out): measure first-byte streaming latency and completion p50/p95/p99 at 20 RPS, 40 concurrent sessions.
2) Long-turn chat (6k in / 1k out): measure completion latency and memory/KV-cache behavior, run at 5 RPS, up to 10 concurrent.
3) Stress run: scale to 50 RPS (synthetic) for short-turns to validate autoscaling behavior.

Next steps:
- I'll loop in our infra engineer to set up a private pilot and run the baseline off your sample request.
- Can you share the exact distribution of input lengths for the chat flows (histogram of tokens) so we can tune batch windows?
- Do you have any hard SLA requirements besides p95 numbers (e.g., retention/audit, regional routing)?

I'll schedule the baseline run for Wednesday if that works for your team.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
(Attachment: redwood_latency_baseline.pdf)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Looping you both in — FinCo (Aaron + Samantha) asked for a baseline using their sample request and the PoC matrix below. Key asks:
- Run the short-turn chat baseline (1.5k in / 200 out) and long-turn (6k in / 1k out) with streaming enabled. Capture first-byte and completion p50/p95/p99.
- Compare 8k vs 32k context runtimes and note the delta in p95 and memory usage.
- Stress test up to 50 RPS for short-turns to validate autoscaler and tail latency under batching.

Action items for infra/dev:
- Dev: can you wire up the finco_sample_request.json and drive the harness in the linked folder? Please use quantized model variant Q4_x for baseline & the FP16 for comparison. Capture the per-token decode time traces.
- Rishi: please validate KV-cache behavior across sessions — does cache reuse work reliably with their session pattern (many small sessions with long histories)? If reuse drops, note the impact on end-to-end latency.

I'll coordinate scheduling with Aaron for Wed; please confirm ETA for the initial baseline run (I told them Wed afternoon PDT).

— Marissa
